signals.text: SEND Information Report March 2024: Catholic Primary School?

St Vincent de Paul Catholic Primary School SEND Information Report (updated March 2024) Our values: respect, responsibility, positivity, generosity, achievement, aspiration Our mission: ‘Love one another as I have loved you’ The SENCO manages the day to day provision for our children with SEND.
Provision for children with SEND is constantly under review and amended where and when necessary.
We monitor the quality of our provision, together with the progress and well-being of children with SEND.

The SENCO holds provision meetings (during staff meetings and individually) to support teachers setting new termly targets on children’s Learning plans (Learning plans are shared with support staff via Edukey).

pageCache.text:
Social Wall
Catholic Life
We are proud of our Catholic ethos and tradition, which we celebrate regularly with collective worship and Mass on feast days and holy days of obligation.
We are very privileged and fortunate to be the parish school of both Westminster Cathedral, the mother church for Catholics in England and Wales, and Holy Apostles, Pimlico. Chaplains from both parishes are regular visitors to the school leading worship and services and throughout the year, the school attends both churches for important feasts and celebrations such as Christmas and Easter.
We are also grateful for the continuing influence and support from our founders, the Daughters of Charity of St Vincent de Paul. You can learn more about the history of the school by clicking HERE
The Catholic Life of the school was judged to be 'outstanding' when we were inspected in 2019. Inspectors commented that: "The school's values and vision statement permeate life at St Vincent de Paul. They are lived out in a very real way by the whole school community."
You can read the report in full HERE
For further information about Westminster Cathedral, click HERE

Saint John Southworth Catholic Academy Trust
The Saint John Southworth Catholic Academy Trust was established in September 2021 with the aim of creating a community of schools in line with the Diocesan vision, built in solidarity to give our pupils the resources to grow whilst receiving an outstanding Catholic education.
Walking in the footsteps of our patron Saint John Southworth, we are a community of faith and love grounded in dignity, service, and perseverance.
St Vincent de Paul converted to academy status on 1 April 2026 and joined the Saint John Southworth Catholic Academy Trust. Saint John Southworth Foundation
The Saint John Southworth Foundation (charity number 1121531) is a registered charity established to provide long-term financial support for the continuing development of all of the schools within the Saint John Southworth Catholic Academy Trust.
To learn more about the Foundation's work and how it supports our schools, visit the website here.
More details about our trust can be found here.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Vincent de Paul Catholic Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Social Wall
Welcome to St Vincent de Paul Catholic Primary School
I am delighted to welcome you to our website. I hope you will enjoy exploring the site and finding out useful and important information and news about our wonderful school. All PDF documents on the site can be read in the viewer or downloaded and printed separately. If you require a paper copy of any document, please contact the school office.
We are a thriving one-form-entry primary school, uniquely located in the shadow of Westminster Cathedral, with whom we maintain close links as the parish school. We are also the parish school of Holy Apostles', Pimlico, following the amalgamation of our school with Westminster Cathedral primary school in 2022. In April 2026, we joined the St John Southworth Catholic Academy Trust.
In 2025 we celebrated 50 years of St Vincent de Paul school at Morpeth Terrace. However, the school has existed in Victoria for 165 years and we are proud to continue the legacy left by the Daughters of Charity, who founded the school in 1859. You can read an overview of the school's history by clicking the button at the bottom of this page.
Today, we provide an education with a distinct Catholic identity for children aged 3 to 11 years. Ours is a warm and friendly school where our shared faith is celebrated through prayer, child-centred liturgies and assemblies.
Our mission statement comes directly from Christ’s words of ‘Love one another as I have loved you,’ and we seek to promote this message in all that we do. We value strongly our partnership with parents in working together to achieve the best outcomes for our children.
Children at St Vincent de Paul are educated in a well-disciplined, caring environment following National Curriculum and the Diocese of Westminster’s guidelines. This enables them to reach high standards that will prepare them for further education when they move onto secondary school and beyond. Outcomes for our pupils at the end of each phase consistently exceed national averages. You can view our latest performance data HERE
If you are interested in a place for your child in any of our year groups or would like to visit the school, please arrange an appointment by contacting the main office by telephone on 020 3351 5990 or by email using: admissions@svpschool.co.uk
We will be pleased to welcome you.
Mr N Scott Cree MA NPQELHead Teacher

Make A Regular Donation
Thank you for wishing to support our school via the Love one Another Fund.
As we launch the Love One Another Fund, we invite members of our community to help support the future of our school. Fundraising plays an important role in bridging the gap between government funding. Regular pledged gifts will help us plan confidently for the future and continue to enrich school life for every child.
Regular gifts of all sizes are welcomed and valued as overtime they grow into substantial amounts. It is the act of giving that draws our community more tightly together.
Please complete this pledge form and set up a regular standing order with your bank. Email the Pledge Form to Anna Carpmael from our Development Office or send the form into Reception.
